text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- A council for the southern town of Tartu was formed by the Reform and Centre parties and the Tartu 2000 electoral bloc.

- The Bank of Estonia published the state inspection report on the bank with some deletions. The report said the bank's actions resulted in a loss of 562.9 million kroons. The wrongdoings included selling gold at a loss and buying it at a higher price. The central bank rejected the report.
- The Reform Party called for a reduction of vehicles of government and local government institutions.
- Tallinn government plans to borrow 240 million kroons next year and to introduce a one-percent tax on sales.
- Estonian Transport Minister Raivo Vare presented Estonia's transit opportunities at a fair in Moscow.
- The sale of tickets to Michael Jackson's concert will begin on Monday.
- Parliament is debating the motor vehicle tax. Some members oppose the introduction of the tax.
- The Tartu University will decide on Monday, whether it will expel foreign students, who have refused to pay tuition fees after the university raised them.
- The government has agreed to exempt companies investments in assets from income tax from 1998.
- The police will receive the new Mazda patrol cars in September instead of July.
